title: Learner 01 | Day 132: Working increment: MCP, integration boundaries, and agent security
body:
## Goal

Expose a small read-only knowledge tool through MCP and integrate it through the existing policy layer.

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/core/values/mcp_tools.py`

**Method/unit:** `validate_source_deletion`

**Why here:** This is a value boundary: it defines accepted values and rejects invalid local data. It must not import HTTP, storage, or model SDK code.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** Protocol errors are handled; tools remain scoped; transport authentication never replaces action authorization.

**Boundaries:** Keep value checks local; no transport/storage/model calls.

## Research hints

1. Research **one observed gap in MCP roles and protocol boundaries / Audit trails, retention, and deletion**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:modelcontextprotocol.io one observed gap in MCP roles and protocol boundaries Audit trails retention`; use [MCP introduction](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** For this increment — Add a pluggable local-model option and an image-description draft flow while keeping text-only operation available. — where are the input, state, failure, and output boundaries? Which trade-off did you choose?

**Review with @Rohan5607:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.
